subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should a processing session with no tracked active work stay recovery-eligible as stale state, or should OpenClaw require stronger no-progress proof before stuck-session recovery can abort it?
rationale: The source path is real, but the current recovery behavior also intentionally reclaims leaked active runs; choosing the safer boundary requires maintainer policy and live evidence, not an automatic classifier-only patch.

options.title: Require live proof before changing recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open until a current-main run captures `state=processing`, `classification=stale_session_state`, and the resulting recovery action under an induced event-loop stall.

options.title: Change processing fallback now
options.body: Treat processing/no-active-work as long-running or stalled-but-observe-only unless a separate active-run progress threshold proves it is stale.

options.title: Preserve current recovery policy
options.body: Accept that processing/no-active-work is recoverable stale state and ask reporters to file only fully reproduced false-abort traces.

recommendation.title: Require live proof before changing recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a current-main run captures `state=processing`, `classification=stale_session_state`, and the resulting recovery action under an induced event-loop stall.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the classifier surface and have adjacent stuck-session recovery history, making them the best available owner for the policy call.
